jobs.description:
Location:
Oriskany, NY (Onsite)
ABOUT Bonide

With a legacy of trust dating back to 1926, Bonide has evolved into a global force in the gardening industry as a proud member of the Syngenta Group. This partnership has bestowed upon our family business the invaluable advantage of a worldwide presence and extensive resources, enabling us to serve gardeners across the globe with exceptional pest control solutions for generations to come. At our Oriskany, NY facility, a dedicated team of over 200 professionals passionately produces our diverse portfolio of synthetic and Organic Gardening Products.
Our commitment to meeting every gardener's needs is unwavering, and we offer a comprehensive range of weed, insect, disease, and animal controls in various formulations and applications. You can find our premium products at national, regional, and local home centers, hardware stores, mass merchants, and garden centers throughout America. Bonide stands tall as a recognized and respected industry leader, reflecting the trust and admiration we have earned from gardening enthusiasts across the country!
Role Summary

The CEO is responsible for short and long-term growth and profitability of Bonide Operations. The position requires an understanding of the local and global markets, latest industry trends, and competitive market strategies.
This candidate will develop, direct and coordinate a local organization with functional responsibility for sales, marketing, business development, regulatory, product management, operations, people, finance, and administration.
The success of the position is measured by increasing the unit´s business value which is measured, amongst other things, by increasing sales in existing accounts, by sales growth with new customers and markets as well as meeting pre-established operational performance objectives while meeting overall business profitability goals.
Key Accountabilities And Responsibilities

Manage the continued growth and evolution of a well-established and profitable business.
Work closely with the existing management team to ensure that both short and long-term objectives are delivered.
Work with the Management team to develop, align and implement on strategic and tactical plans, including the annual WorkPlan, 5-Years Plan and the budget including the execution of these plans.
Demonstrate an in-depth knowledge of the marketplace, key dynamics, and company policies as well as up-to-date knowledge of the key competitors and their likely strategies.
Manage P&L including the delivery of top line and bottom-line results; driving the company to achieve and surpass sales, profitability, cash flow and business goals and objectives.
Execute established goals for sales growth, market share, profit contribution and return on investment to achieve results stated in approved plan.
Ensure gross margin required by the business through achieving the right balance between sales volume and profitability through a classification of the portfolio.
Establish organizational structure, identify and appoint functional staff leaders.
Create and maintain relationships with customers at all levels of the organization.
Ensure proper management of working capital (inventories and product availability), through active participation in planning meetings and providing quality and timely information to the production, logistics and procurement areas.
Report the unit’s financial results both on monthly and quarterly basis according to the global guidelines.
Expected to recruit and manage staff, including performance monitoring, mentoring, and training.
Engage, motivate and develop the employee population.

MEASURES OF SUCCESS

People Development: Drive sustained improvement in engagement and enablement, as measured through the Employee Engagement Survey (EES). Build and enhance commercial skills by driving continuous improvement of mindset/environment to create innovative tools for simplicity & effectiveness.
Financial Execution: Drive the sales and profit growth of the business and ensure the WorkPlan goals are achieved. Manage operational effectiveness by working closely with the finance business partner to understand OPEX and EBIT implications.
Strategy: Spearhead the development, communication and implementation of effective growth strategies and processes. Understand the local and global markets, latest industry trends, and competitive market strategies. Monitor sales and market trends through publications and customer contact.
Customer Focus: Develop good relationships, networks with staff, customers, and industry peers. Ensure that local business strategy aligns, where possible, with the global initiatives
Strategy: Demonstrate strategic mindset to be able to effectively position the company against the competitors while evaluating risks and business trade-offs.
Critical Experiences For Success

To be successful in this role you will have/be:
Ability to collaborate and develop strong relationships with all levels of personnel.
Proven experience directly managing a Profit and Loss (P&L) statement of at least $50M.
Demonstrated success managing multi-channel portfolios (Distributor, Mass/Big-box, E-commerce)
Strong commercial awareness, operations/manufacturing oversite, project management and team leadership.
Background in branded CPG, home improvement, lawn & garden, or adjacent categories preferred
Demonstrate sense of urgency and time effectiveness.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to lead and influence key decision makers.
Identify, evaluate and communicate risks and opportunities on a timely basis.
Build and foster solid business partnering relationships with internal and external customers.
Demonstrate ADAMA behaviors: Accountable, Curious, Courageous, and Collaboration.

Travel: Must be able to accommodate up to 20% of domestic and international travels including some overnight and weekend commitments.
Education/Experience

Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration, Entomology, Science, or related field.
MBA/Master’s degree a plus.
10+ years of roles with responsibility over multiple functions including sales/marketing or previous experience as country manager/CEO in the US consumer market

Languages: Fluent in English, both written and Oral communication
The Following Experiences Are Preferred

Strong ability to handle multiple demands and priorities.
Strong presentation and influencing skills.
Strong interpersonal skills and organizational skills.
Strong time management skills.
Strong problem solving, creativity skills, and the ability to exercise sound judgment and make decisions based on accurate and timely analyses.

Other Skills & Abilities: PC proficiency is essential with strong working knowledge of Microsoft office.
FUNCTIONAL EXCELLENCE

Process focused with an understanding of end-to-end business processes and the financial impact.

Ability to manage, motivate and develop people.

jobs.description:
Description

Providence Saint John’s Cancer Institute in Santa Monica
is a world-renowned cancer research and treatment destination dedicated to advancing cancer care through innovative research, leading-edge therapies, and compassionate, patient-centered care. Affiliated with Providence Saint John’s Health Center, the Institute brings together nationally recognized physicians, scientists, and multidisciplinary care teams to deliver groundbreaking treatments and clinical trials across a broad spectrum of cancers. Known for pioneering discoveries that have shaped modern oncology, Saint John’s Cancer Institute remains at the forefront of translational research, education, and innovation, improving outcomes for patients locally and around the world.

Calling All Esteemed Leaders!
Are you a healthcare leader with a passion for advancing cancer care, digestive health services, physician alignment, and patient-centered innovation? Do you thrive in collaborative environments where strategic planning, clinical excellence, and program growth come together to improve care across the continuum? If so, we invite you to explore this leadership opportunity with Providence.

The Role

In partnership with the Executive Medical Director, the Executive Director is accountable for leadership, direction and implementation of the Cancer Institute for Providence Saint John's including development and implementation of a strategic plan in collaboration with aligned and independent stakeholders in Coastal Service Area and additionally will have similar responsibilities for Digestive Health Institute at Saint John's.

Transform delivery of clinical care. Develop and implement program strategies that will provide an exceptional patient-centered experience by developing a seamless care delivery system and innovative care models to improve quality outcomes, reduce unnecessary clinical variation, improve coordination across the continuum, and help implement care consistent with state and national clinical guidelines.

Create enduring alignment with physicians, researchers and clinicians. Create internal and external provider alignment strategies that strengthen seamless and innovative care delivery and achieve the Triple Aim: improved quality, affordability and customer experience.

Thrive under new reimbursement models. Collaborate with Finance and Managed Care to develop program strategies and partner with payers, purchasers and providers to develop reimbursement models that advance seamless and innovative care delivery by rewarding quality, care coordination and value.

Enhance access by improving affordability. Develop and implement program strategies to enhance access to care, clinical effectiveness and improve healthcare affordability by providing value-based care across the continuum and reducing overall administrative and care delivery expenses.

Grow to meet community needs. Create and implement strategies to serve more people throughout the continuum of care via appropriate growth and development of programmatic services in existing and new markets.

What You’ll Do

Develop and successfully implement the Cancer Institute and Digestive Health Institute Strategic Plan including ministry and market-specific growth plans, capital planning and resource allocation across the continuum, in collaboration with Regional, Ministry and physician leadership and other key stakeholders.
Develop and implement a physician alignment and growth strategy across Coastal Area, including medical foundations, medical groups, IPAs, and independent practices.
Develop and oversee Cancer Institute and Digestive Health Institute program operating and capital budgets.
Develop and maintain a balanced scorecard to monitor and measure key program goals and outcomes, including Triple Aim goals (improved quality, affordability, experience), program growth, physician alignment and growth, and other goals that may be established.
Assess market and determine areas of opportunity/threat within program. Based on analysis, develop recommendations for program and service development or expansion.
Evaluate Cancer Institute and Digestive Health Institute programs and services across the continuum. Identify gaps and develop a plan to fill these gaps through developing new programs or collaborating with other organizations.
Collaborate effectively across all Cancer Institute and Digestive Health Institute clinical programs to develop and/or enhance programs and service delivery in a coordinated way to best serve patients and the community.
Responsible for the development and/or implementation of evidence-based, best practice clinical protocols across the organization, in collaboration with Divisional and System collaboratives, to improve health outcomes across the continuum.
Work with key administrative and physician leaders to gain consensus. Provide appropriate support for implementation in conjunction with key stakeholders.
Collaborate with Finance and Managed Care to develop new financing models to connect program strategies in support of affordability, high quality and coordination of care (e.g., bundled payments).
Collaborate with clinical operations to assure the effective and efficient delivery of services including patient satisfaction, physician satisfaction, quality, workforce planning, and standardization.
Responsible for development of tumor site clinical programs in collaboration with Executive Medical Director and in coordination with the site-based Cancer leaders and each organization's respective ELTs.
Define clinical services based on market and data analysis, identify greatest opportunity, and recommend appropriate infrastructure required to support new services and/or models of care.
Develop and coordinate program strategies for delivery of outreach services, including telehealth.
Represent program as a government, business and community liaison.
Represent service lines/programs on key System, Division and Ministry committees to formulate strategies and tactics to achieve clinical performance improvement in healthcare delivery.
Establish priorities for program marketing development and outreach designed to support growth.
Develop and implement research strategies within program, monitor financial and scientific outcomes.
Identify strategic philanthropic priorities and partner with Foundations to achieve targeted goals.
Negotiate and maintain directorship, consultant and other physician agreements.
Assure that all regulatory requirements for the Cancer Institute program are within compliance.
Partner with Philanthropy in raising funds to support strategic initiatives.

What You’ll Bring

Education & Credentials

Bachelor's Degree in Healthcare, Business, or related field.
Master's Degree in Healthcare, Business, Organizational Leadership or related field (preferred).

Experience & Expertise

5 years of progressive management experience in healthcare, preferably with in-depth knowledge specific to clinical program areas across the continuum.
5 years of experience leading teams, group facilitation, event management and project management.
Demonstrated experience and success developing and implementing innovative clinical program growth strategies, physician and payer alignment, and consumer engagement models in a highly competitive and complex market environment.
Experience building clinical programs across the continuum of care, including ambulatory, acute and post-acute care, medical group, home and community-based sites.
Knowledge and understanding of emerging healthcare, market and technology trends, including forces influencing the growth, utilization and delivery of cancer services.
Financial management skills including healthcare budgeting and financing, pricing, revenue optimization, reimbursement and payment models, and cost management.
Familiarity with business intelligence tools including benchmarking best practices, data tracking and monitoring outcomes; experience developing and implementing balanced scorecards. Understands the importance of data quality, transparency and privacy concerns.
Skills in change management, Six Sigma, Lean and/or other continuous performance improvement techniques.
Understand and be comfortable in a complex matrix structured organization.

Professional & Leadership Capabilities

A team player with strong interpersonal and communication skills; track record of developing collaborative and effective working relationships with physicians, clinicians, management, colleagues and peers; ability to motivate, lead and influence others to implement key strategies.
Leadership skills including ability to prioritize and organize work; flexibility and agility to process information and adapt quickly to a changing healthcare environment; create goals and accountability; lead projects from concept to implementation in a timely manner; and achieve results.
Demonstrated experience creating a culture of excellence, including quality and service improvement.
Strong customer focus with physicians, management, colleagues, internal and external stakeholders.
Team training and facilitated leadership skills.
Strong professional ethics including a commitment to advance Providence's Mission, Vision and Core Values.
Must possess strong self-motivational skills and be able to function independently without direct supervision while involving and requesting assistance from various leaders as appropriate.
Strong strategic planning, business development, physician relations, project management and business skills.
Strong communications, interpersonal relations and team building skills are a requirement for internal and external purposes.

Why Join Us?

Institute Leadership: Provide leadership for the Cancer Institute at Providence Saint John's, as well as the Digestive Health Institute at Saint John's .
Strategic Growth & Innovation: Lead strategic planning, physician alignment, program growth, outreach expansion, and development of innovative models of care across the continuum.
Clinical Excellence: Advance evidence-based clinical protocols, care coordination, quality outcomes, affordability, and patient-centered care.
Collaborative Impact: Partner with physicians, researchers, clinicians, operational leaders, payers, Foundations, and community stakeholders to help achieve the Triple Aim of improved quality, affordability, and customer experience.

Ready to Shape the Future of Healthcare?

If you are a strategic healthcare leader with experience in program development, physician alignment, clinical operations, and healthcare transformation, we encourage you to apply and help advance cancer and digestive health services across Providence.

jobs.description:
The Chief Executive Officer
is an accomplished, relationship-driven leader with expertise in mobilizing capital, building and stewarding institutional relationships, stakeholder engagement, and organizational growth, paired with a strong commitment to Hawaiʻi and its communities.

ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION

Hawaiʻi Community Lending (HCL) is a nonprofit Native Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) and licensed mortgage lender and servicer dedicated to expanding access to credit and capital for Native Hawaiians and other underserved communities throughout Hawaiʻi. Founded in 2002 and independent since 2014, HCL grew from a community-driven effort to address barriers to affordable homeownership into a sophisticated, statewide community development finance institution. Guided by the philosophy of kahua waiwai , or “foundation of wealth,” HCL views stable housing and financial security as foundations for family stability, cultural connection, community well-being, and intergenerational prosperity. Its model combines flexible lending with financial education, technical assistance, and long-term relationships with borrowers and community partners.

HCL has established an affordable homeownership system that provides financing for homebuilders to homebuyers to homeowners including debt consolidation and credit builder loans, mortgage and construction financing, home repair and rehabilitation, and small business lending. The organization has developed specialized expertise in financing homes on Hawaiian Home Lands, supporting families facing financial hardship, preserving homeownership, and filling gaps left by conventional lenders. Since its inception, HCL has helped more than 6,500 Hawaiʻi households access over $203 million in grants, loans, and mortgage financing. Its capacity to respond at scale was demonstrated during COVID-19, when HCL was entrusted with approximately $40 million to help thousands of families avoid foreclosure and eviction, and more recently through its support for families and communities affected by the Lahaina wildfires and Kona Low, Lala, and Lowell tropical storms.

Today, HCL is well-positioned to scale dramatically in its next chapter. The organization has grown from a $3 million fund in 2020 to approximately $25 million and has built the lending, servicing, financial, and organizational infrastructure needed for accelerated growth. With deep community relationships, experienced leadership, and growing local and national recognition, HCL has the potential to become a $100+ million fund within five years while maintaining strong financial performance and meaningful community impact. This growth would enable HCL to mobilize significantly more capital, reach more families, strengthen a new affordable homeownership system, and demonstrate the power of mission-driven finance to create lasting economic opportunity and prevent outmigration of Hawaiʻi residents.

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

The Chief Executive Officer will lead HCL into its next chapter, building upon a strong foundation while helping define the organization’s ambition, reach, and influence for years to come. This is an opportunity to lead a distinctive financial institution at the intersection of affordable homeownership, community development, and economic opportunity, and to shape how capital can be deployed more effectively to serve Hawaiʻi’s families and communities. In partnership with the Board and executive team, the CEO will establish HCL's strategic direction, translate it into clear priorities and measurable results, and ensure HCL has the leadership, resources, and organizational capacity to grow responsibly.

A central mandate will be to expand and diversify the capital available to HCL, strengthening the financial foundation for its next phase of growth. The CEO will be a trusted and highly visible representative of HCL to banks, investors, foundations, corporations, government agencies, Native Hawaiian institutions, and other mission-aligned partners. Grounded in credibility, authenticity, and a deep understanding of HCL’s mission, the CEO will open doors to new sources of capital, innovative financing opportunities, and strategic partnerships. The successful candidate will be energized by bringing people and institutions together around a compelling purpose and inspiring confidence in HCL’s vision and continued growth.

The CEO will also guide HCL’s strategic expansion, identifying opportunities to extend its reach while maintaining the financial strength, risk discipline, and community accountability that have enabled its success. Building on HCL’s established lending platform, the CEO will advance opportunities in affordable homeownership, housing and construction finance, small business lending, and other areas where flexible, mission-driven capital can address unmet need. The leader will bring an enterprise perspective to growth, balancing opportunity with financial sustainability and ensuring that new initiatives are supported by the appropriate capital, infrastructure, talent, and capabilities. As HCL’s chief external voice, the CEO will elevate the organization’s profile and influence locally and nationally, helping shape the broader policy and financing environment in which HCL operates. The role will include engaging policymakers, public agencies, Native Hawaiian institutions, community leaders, funders, financial institutions, and industry partners to advance policies and resources that expand access to housing and capital. Internally, the CEO will foster a high-performing, collaborative culture, partner effectively with the Board and executive team, and ensure the organization remains focused on both strong performance and meaningful community outcomes. Ultimately, the opportunity is to help shape not only HCL’s future, but the broader ecosystem of capital and opportunity available to Hawaiʻi’s communities.

The ideal candidate will be an accomplished, highly relational executive who combines strategic vision, financial acumen, and executive leadership with a genuine commitment to Hawaiʻi and its communities. They will have demonstrated success mobilizing capital, building and stewarding institutional relationships, leading through an experienced executive team, and working effectively with a Board and diverse external stakeholders. Candidates may come from banking, community development finance, affordable housing, commercial or mortgage lending, impact investing, philanthropy, economic development, or another mission-driven financial environment; direct CDFI experience is valuable but not essential. Above all, HCL seeks a leader who leads with integrity and cultural humility, earns trust authentically, and is inspired by the opportunity to use capital, relationships, and leadership to create greater housing and economic opportunity for generations of Hawaiʻi families.

Target Annual Salary: $250,000 - $275,000

Please submit the following, addressed to Hawaiʻi Community Lending Search Committee, c/o Inkinen Executive Search, via email to executives@inkinen.com by October 23, 2026:
Cover Letter – expressing the reason for your interest in Hawaiʻi Community Lending, and how your skills and experiences match the CEO role.

Position Summary:

Florida Atlantic University seeks an experienced fundraising leader looking to grow their career and join a relationship-focused, results-oriented, donor-centered advancement team.

Opened in 1964, Florida Atlantic University serves more than 30,000 students across six beautiful campuses in South Florida. The College of Social Work and Criminal Justice inspires and prepares ethical, culturally competent, and innovative professionals who analyze, implement, and evaluate criminal justice and social welfare policies, practices, and technologies; provide direct services to populations in need; and promote wellness and well-being for individuals, families, and communities in South Florida and beyond.

The Associate Director of Advancement for the College of Social Work and Criminal Justice
at Florida Atlantic University works collaboratively with the Dean, Associate and Assistant Deans, and faculty, and under the supervision of an Assistant Vice President for Institutional Advancement or/and a Director of Advancement. The Associate Director plans and implements a comprehensive strategic fundraising plan to meet the educational and programmatic missions and activities of the College of Social Work and Criminal Justice and its areas. The Associate Director qualifies, cultivates, solicits, and stewards a portfolio of donors and prospective donors with the inclination and capacity to make five- to six-figure gifts to the College of Social Work and Criminal Justice at FAU.

The successful candidate will experience a commitment to Advancement at the very top from the President; a seasoned, dynamic Vice President of Institutional Advancement with a winning track record; an innovative and committed Dean at the College of Social Work and Criminal Justice; and the opportunities and responsibilities appropriate for fundraising leaders to complete Florida Atlantic’s next campaign.

Summary of Responsibilities:

Develop and implement comprehensive cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies for individual major, legacy, and principal gift prospects assigned. Work both independently and in concert with Institutional Advancement colleagues to implement strategies leading to direct solicitation of five- to six-figure gifts.
Build a strong pipeline of alumni and other prospective donors to expand the portfolio of qualified prospects for gifts of five- to six-figure amounts.
Create and execute solicitation and closure strategies for major gifts aligned with the College of Social Work and Criminal Justice and University fundraising priorities and campaigns, measured against the attainment of personal metrics associated with the position.
Collaborate with the Dean, department chairs, and faculty to identify funding priorities, assess relevance and feasibility for proposed project/priority, and develop and manage comprehensive strategies to secure gifts for selected priorities.
Devise individualized involvement/engagement strategies for all prospects using an approach that ensures that most highly rated prospects receive the most attention.
Advise the Institutional Advancement’s Legacy Giving Office of prospects with an interest in a planned gift and work collaboratively to devise an overall strategy for cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding planned gift donors.
In concert with Institutional Advancement colleagues, oversee the preparation of necessary materials including concept papers, funding proposals, briefings for FAU leadership and board members when necessary, and scheduled stewardship reports, for all assigned prospects.
Identify prospects to participate on boards, committees, or other programs that promote the cultivation process.
Assist the Advancement team on special assignments to ensure long-term donor engagement and retention and support the Annual Giving team to successfully implement the College’s annual campaign.
Partner with the Donor Relations and Stewardship Office to ensure appropriate stewardship is provided to donors on existing endowment and current-use funds.
Facilitate effective communication between the College of Social Work and Criminal Justice and its programs, and the division of Institutional Advancement.
Participate and assist in planning signature events at the University, within the College, and in the community that provide opportunities for strategic engagement with prospects and donors.
Work closely with the College’s Dean and manage the advancement/fundraising function of the College of Social Work and Criminal Justice Advisory Board; act as a liaison to the Board and to the Office of Institutional Advancement on policies, procedures, and approvals.
In conjunction with the College’s scholarship contacts, oversee that all donor outcomes related to scholarships, such as thank-you notes, event attendance, and in-person visits, are executed in a timely manner.
Participate in weekly meetings with the Dean to discuss donors and other fundraising priorities with the College of Social Work and Criminal Justice.
Work closely with a team of advancement and alumni engagement colleagues in the College of Social Work and Criminal Justice.

Pendo is seeking a strategic, proactive Chief of Staff to serve as a trusted advisor and partner to our CEO. This highly visible role will help shape and advance company priorities, drive cross-functional alignment, and enable effective decision-making across the executive team. You’ll bring an independent and balanced point of view, build trusted relationships across the organization, and help translate the CEO’s and executive team’s priorities into meaningful business outcomes.

This role is based in our Raleigh office and requires travel.

What This Looks Like Day-to-day

Honestly, there is no day-to-day for this job -- that’s the point. We’re looking for a heat-seeking missile to direct at the company’s hardest problems. Yes, you’ll be a member of our C-team helping to maximize our team’s entire effectiveness including our strategy planning, goal-setting, etc. We’re not looking for a facilitator or agenda-creator. We’re looking for someone who can synthesize data, form opinions and tackle problems with minimal supervision.

Strategic planning and operating cadence: Drive the company’s strategic planning and operating rhythm, including annual thematic goals and quarterly OKRs. Partner with executive leaders and program owners to establish priorities, track progress, and surface issues requiring leadership attention.
Tackle the hard problems: Take on complex, high-impact problems with minimal direction. Identify root causes, bring together the right perspectives to shape the path forward, and drive the work to a measurable outcome.
Turn executive priorities into measurable results: Translate critical priorities into coordinated action across the organization. Mobilize the right leaders, remove obstacles, establish accountability, and sustain momentum through delivery.
Executive and board communications: Develop high-quality narratives and materials for board, investor, executive, and other high-stakes meetings. Distill complex information into clear, compelling communication tailored to the audience and desired outcome.
Leadership meetings and offsites: Lead executive team meetings and offsites in close partnership with the CEO. Shape agendas around the highest-leverage business issues and facilitate focused discussion, debate, and decision-making.

Who You Are

Beyond the qualifications, we hire through a specific lens. These aren't buzzwords; they're the things we'll actually look for in how you talk about your work.

You're a builder, not a maintainer.

You're most energized when there isn't a clear path yet, and you get to define it. You don't wait for direction; you identify gaps, shape solutions, and drive them forward. At Pendo, great Chiefs of Staff don't just follow instructions; they operate as strategic advisors, influencing decisions, guiding stakeholders, and elevating how we work.

You're AI-curious

You're not using AI tools occasionally. You're rewiring how you work around them. You're faster, sharper, and more prolific because of it, and you bring that energy to everything — how you approach your work, how you prep, how you communicate, how you think. We want someone who sees AI as a multiplier, not a shortcut.

Progressive experience in a technology, top-tier consulting, investing, or another high-performance environment.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce decision-ready presentations and board materials.

Experience across multiple company stages, from early growth through scaled operations.
A combination of consulting, investing, or strategy experience and hands-on operating leadership.
Experience with enterprise transformation, operating-model design, product-led growth, or multi-product SaaS.

About Pendo

Pendo was founded in 2013 by former product managers, who combined their heads and hearts to build something they wanted but never had as product managers: a simple way to understand and attack what truly drives product success. Our mission is to improve society's experience with software. Come join one of the fastest-growing startups, supported by best-in-class institutions like Battery Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, Spark Capital and Meritech.

The Chief Executive Officer
is an accomplished, relationship-driven leader with expertise in mobilizing capital, building and stewarding institutional relationships, stakeholder engagement, and organizational growth, paired with a strong commitment to Hawaiʻi and its communities.

ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION

Hawaiʻi Community Lending (HCL) is a nonprofit Native Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) and licensed mortgage lender and servicer dedicated to expanding access to credit and capital for Native Hawaiians and other underserved communities throughout Hawaiʻi. Founded in 2002 and independent since 2014, HCL grew from a community-driven effort to address barriers to affordable homeownership into a sophisticated, statewide community development finance institution. Guided by the philosophy of kahua waiwai , or “foundation of wealth,” HCL views stable housing and financial security as foundations for family stability, cultural connection, community well-being, and intergenerational prosperity. Its model combines flexible lending with financial education, technical assistance, and long-term relationships with borrowers and community partners.

HCL has established an affordable homeownership system that provides financing for homebuilders to homebuyers to homeowners including debt consolidation and credit builder loans, mortgage and construction financing, home repair and rehabilitation, and small business lending. The organization has developed specialized expertise in financing homes on Hawaiian Home Lands, supporting families facing financial hardship, preserving homeownership, and filling gaps left by conventional lenders. Since its inception, HCL has helped more than 6,500 Hawaiʻi households access over $203 million in grants, loans, and mortgage financing. Its capacity to respond at scale was demonstrated during COVID-19, when HCL was entrusted with approximately $40 million to help thousands of families avoid foreclosure and eviction, and more recently through its support for families and communities affected by the Lahaina wildfires and Kona Low, Lala, and Lowell tropical storms.

Today, HCL is well-positioned to scale dramatically in its next chapter. The organization has grown from a $3 million fund in 2020 to approximately $25 million and has built the lending, servicing, financial, and organizational infrastructure needed for accelerated growth. With deep community relationships, experienced leadership, and growing local and national recognition, HCL has the potential to become a $100+ million fund within five years while maintaining strong financial performance and meaningful community impact. This growth would enable HCL to mobilize significantly more capital, reach more families, strengthen a new affordable homeownership system, and demonstrate the power of mission-driven finance to create lasting economic opportunity and prevent outmigration of Hawaiʻi residents.

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

The Chief Executive Officer will lead HCL into its next chapter, building upon a strong foundation while helping define the organization’s ambition, reach, and influence for years to come. This is an opportunity to lead a distinctive financial institution at the intersection of affordable homeownership, community development, and economic opportunity, and to shape how capital can be deployed more effectively to serve Hawaiʻi’s families and communities. In partnership with the Board and executive team, the CEO will establish HCL's strategic direction, translate it into clear priorities and measurable results, and ensure HCL has the leadership, resources, and organizational capacity to grow responsibly.

A central mandate will be to expand and diversify the capital available to HCL, strengthening the financial foundation for its next phase of growth. The CEO will be a trusted and highly visible representative of HCL to banks, investors, foundations, corporations, government agencies, Native Hawaiian institutions, and other mission-aligned partners. Grounded in credibility, authenticity, and a deep understanding of HCL’s mission, the CEO will open doors to new sources of capital, innovative financing opportunities, and strategic partnerships. The successful candidate will be energized by bringing people and institutions together around a compelling purpose and inspiring confidence in HCL’s vision and continued growth.

The CEO will also guide HCL’s strategic expansion, identifying opportunities to extend its reach while maintaining the financial strength, risk discipline, and community accountability that have enabled its success. Building on HCL’s established lending platform, the CEO will advance opportunities in affordable homeownership, housing and construction finance, small business lending, and other areas where flexible, mission-driven capital can address unmet need. The leader will bring an enterprise perspective to growth, balancing opportunity with financial sustainability and ensuring that new initiatives are supported by the appropriate capital, infrastructure, talent, and capabilities. As HCL’s chief external voice, the CEO will elevate the organization’s profile and influence locally and nationally, helping shape the broader policy and financing environment in which HCL operates. The role will include engaging policymakers, public agencies, Native Hawaiian institutions, community leaders, funders, financial institutions, and industry partners to advance policies and resources that expand access to housing and capital. Internally, the CEO will foster a high-performing, collaborative culture, partner effectively with the Board and executive team, and ensure the organization remains focused on both strong performance and meaningful community outcomes. Ultimately, the opportunity is to help shape not only HCL’s future, but the broader ecosystem of capital and opportunity available to Hawaiʻi’s communities.

The ideal candidate will be an accomplished, highly relational executive who combines strategic vision, financial acumen, and executive leadership with a genuine commitment to Hawaiʻi and its communities. They will have demonstrated success mobilizing capital, building and stewarding institutional relationships, leading through an experienced executive team, and working effectively with a Board and diverse external stakeholders. Candidates may come from banking, community development finance, affordable housing, commercial or mortgage lending, impact investing, philanthropy, economic development, or another mission-driven financial environment; direct CDFI experience is valuable but not essential. Above all, HCL seeks a leader who leads with integrity and cultural humility, earns trust authentically, and is inspired by the opportunity to use capital, relationships, and leadership to create greater housing and economic opportunity for generations of Hawaiʻi families.

Target Annual Salary: $250,000 - $275,000

Position Summary:

Florida Atlantic University seeks an experienced fundraising leader looking to grow their career and join a relationship-focused, results-oriented, donor-centered advancement team.

Opened in 1964, Florida Atlantic University serves more than 30,000 students across six beautiful campuses in South Florida. The College of Social Work and Criminal Justice inspires and prepares ethical, culturally competent, and innovative professionals who analyze, implement, and evaluate criminal justice and social welfare policies, practices, and technologies; provide direct services to populations in need; and promote wellness and well-being for individuals, families, and communities in South Florida and beyond.

The Associate Director of Advancement for the College of Social Work and Criminal Justice
at Florida Atlantic University works collaboratively with the Dean, Associate and Assistant Deans, and faculty, and under the supervision of an Assistant Vice President for Institutional Advancement or/and a Director of Advancement. The Associate Director plans and implements a comprehensive strategic fundraising plan to meet the educational and programmatic missions and activities of the College of Social Work and Criminal Justice and its areas. The Associate Director qualifies, cultivates, solicits, and stewards a portfolio of donors and prospective donors with the inclination and capacity to make five- to six-figure gifts to the College of Social Work and Criminal Justice at FAU.

The successful candidate will experience a commitment to Advancement at the very top from the President; a seasoned, dynamic Vice President of Institutional Advancement with a winning track record; an innovative and committed Dean at the College of Social Work and Criminal Justice; and the opportunities and responsibilities appropriate for fundraising leaders to complete Florida Atlantic’s next campaign.

Summary of Responsibilities:

Develop and implement comprehensive cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies for individual major, legacy, and principal gift prospects assigned. Work both independently and in concert with Institutional Advancement colleagues to implement strategies leading to direct solicitation of five- to six-figure gifts.
Build a strong pipeline of alumni and other prospective donors to expand the portfolio of qualified prospects for gifts of five- to six-figure amounts.
Create and execute solicitation and closure strategies for major gifts aligned with the College of Social Work and Criminal Justice and University fundraising priorities and campaigns, measured against the attainment of personal metrics associated with the position.
Collaborate with the Dean, department chairs, and faculty to identify funding priorities, assess relevance and feasibility for proposed project/priority, and develop and manage comprehensive strategies to secure gifts for selected priorities.
Devise individualized involvement/engagement strategies for all prospects using an approach that ensures that most highly rated prospects receive the most attention.
Advise the Institutional Advancement’s Legacy Giving Office of prospects with an interest in a planned gift and work collaboratively to devise an overall strategy for cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding planned gift donors.
In concert with Institutional Advancement colleagues, oversee the preparation of necessary materials including concept papers, funding proposals, briefings for FAU leadership and board members when necessary, and scheduled stewardship reports, for all assigned prospects.
Identify prospects to participate on boards, committees, or other programs that promote the cultivation process.
Assist the Advancement team on special assignments to ensure long-term donor engagement and retention and support the Annual Giving team to successfully implement the College’s annual campaign.
Partner with the Donor Relations and Stewardship Office to ensure appropriate stewardship is provided to donors on existing endowment and current-use funds.
Facilitate effective communication between the College of Social Work and Criminal Justice and its programs, and the division of Institutional Advancement.
Participate and assist in planning signature events at the University, within the College, and in the community that provide opportunities for strategic engagement with prospects and donors.
Work closely with the College’s Dean and manage the advancement/fundraising function of the College of Social Work and Criminal Justice Advisory Board; act as a liaison to the Board and to the Office of Institutional Advancement on policies, procedures, and approvals.
In conjunction with the College’s scholarship contacts, oversee that all donor outcomes related to scholarships, such as thank-you notes, event attendance, and in-person visits, are executed in a timely manner.

new_jobs.title: Chief of Staff, CEO
new_jobs.description:
Pendo is seeking a strategic, proactive Chief of Staff to serve as a trusted advisor and partner to our CEO. This highly visible role will help shape and advance company priorities, drive cross-functional alignment, and enable effective decision-making across the executive team. The ideal candidate is a sharp, analytical thinker who thrives in complexity, brings clarity to ambiguous situations, and moves seamlessly between strategy and execution. You’ll bring an independent and balanced point of view, build trusted relationships across the organization, and help translate the CEO’s and executive team’s priorities into meaningful business outcomes.

This role is based in our Raleigh office and requires travel.

What This Looks Like Day-to-day

Honestly, there is no day-to-day for this job -- that’s the point. We’re looking for a heat-seeking missile to direct at the company’s hardest problems. Yes, you’ll be a member of our C-team helping to maximize our team’s entire effectiveness including our strategy planning, goal-setting, etc. We’re not looking for a facilitator or agenda-creator. We’re looking for someone who can synthesize data, form opinions and tackle problems with minimal supervision.

Strategic planning and operating cadence: Drive the company’s strategic planning and operating rhythm, including annual thematic goals and quarterly OKRs. Partner with executive leaders and program owners to establish priorities, track progress, and surface issues requiring leadership attention.
Tackle the hard problems: Take on complex, high-impact problems with minimal direction. Identify root causes, bring together the right perspectives to shape the path forward, and drive the work to a measurable outcome.
Turn executive priorities into measurable results: Translate critical priorities into coordinated action across the organization. Mobilize the right leaders, remove obstacles, establish accountability, and sustain momentum through delivery.
Executive and board communications: Develop high-quality narratives and materials for board, investor, executive, and other high-stakes meetings. Distill complex information into clear, compelling communication tailored to the audience and desired outcome.
Leadership meetings and offsites: Lead executive team meetings and offsites in close partnership with the CEO. Shape agendas around the highest-leverage business issues and facilitate focused discussion, debate, and decision-making.

Who You Are

Beyond the qualifications, we hire through a specific lens. These aren't buzzwords; they're the things we'll actually look for in how you talk about your work.

You're a builder, not a maintainer.

You're most energized when there isn't a clear path yet, and you get to define it. You don't wait for direction; you identify gaps, shape solutions, and drive them forward. At Pendo, great Chiefs of Staff don't just follow instructions; they operate as strategic advisors, influencing decisions, guiding stakeholders, and elevating how we work.

You're AI-curious

You're not using AI tools occasionally. You're rewiring how you work around them. You're faster, sharper, and more prolific because of it, and you bring that energy to everything — how you approach your work, how you prep, how you communicate, how you think. We want someone who sees AI as a multiplier, not a shortcut.

Must-haves

Progressive experience in a technology, top-tier consulting, investing, or another high-performance environment.
Experience partnering directly with a founder, CEO, or senior executive and personally owning enterprise-level initiatives from strategy through implementation.
A track record of delivering measurable cross-functional business outcomes across complex, senior-stakeholder environments.
Strong understanding of how product, go-to-market, customer experience, finance, and operations work together.
Exceptional strategic judgment and analytical ability, including the ability to make sound recommendations with incomplete information.
Executive presence with the ability to influence, align, and constructively challenge senior stakeholders.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce decision-ready presentations and board materials.

Nice-to-haves

Experience across multiple company stages, from early growth through scaled operations.
A combination of consulting, investing, or strategy experience and hands-on operating leadership.
Experience with enterprise transformation, operating-model design, product-led growth, or multi-product SaaS.

About Pendo

Pendo was founded in 2013 by former product managers, who combined their heads and hearts to build something they wanted but never had as product managers: a simple way to understand and attack what truly drives product success. Our mission is to improve society's experience with software. Come join one of the fastest-growing startups, supported by best-in-class institutions like Battery Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, Spark Capital and Meritech.

Pendo Core Values:
Bias to Act, Hone Your Craft, The Team is Pendo, and Maniacal Focus.

Location:
Pendo is a hybrid culture. In-office 3 days per week unless designated remote.

Compensation:
The expected salary range for this role to be performed in Raleigh, NC is USD $203,000 - USD $244,000 base plus a bonus target and equity

Benefits:
Pendo offers highly competitive, employer-heavy coverage in the United States, including $0 premium options, strong 401(k) match, equity, and flexible time off.

We are an equal opportunity employer and believe having diverse teams where everyone brings their whole self to Pendo is key to our success. We welcome all people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives.
